condition: acutely incarcerated right inguinal mass presenting with sudden induration and severe pain in an older adult man
level_rationale: Sudden induration and severe pain today in a pre-existing 3-month right groin lump in a 68-year-old man indicates suspected acute inguinal incarceration or strangulation requiring immediate emergency department surgical evaluation to prevent bowel ischemia, whereas that same 3-month right groin lump staying soft and flattening back in whenever lying down describes an uncomplicated reducible groin hernia warranting non-emergent outpatient physician evaluation.

reference_facts.text: Speaker is a 68 year old man
Has had a small lump in his right groin for 3 months
The right groin lump suddenly turned hard and severely painful today

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain older-adult everyday lexical register swap (-reg) + causal belief-addition clause (-att) + same-lump positive reducibility clinic control (-cf).

design_note: Uses three strictly atomic reference facts (68-year-old man, 3-month small right groin lump, and sudden hardening with severe pain today) with a 2-word span difference (10 vs 12 words), zero diagnosis labels ('hernia' omitted), and 11 shared trailing tokens ('and severely painful today so I need to go to the'). Under Rule A first choice, changing only the physical property of that exact 3-month groin lump from acute hardening and severe pain today to staying soft and flattening back in when lying down shifts right care cleanly from ER (level 4) to generalist outpatient evaluation (level 2) with zero stated negatives.
